sophia: Heads-up — Cedar (cust F) just pushed two LoRA merges (v1, v1.1). Requesting a quick compatibility + int4 quant smoke. I'm seeing weird emoji tokenization dropouts in an initial sample.

aj: Which model refs and merge commands did they use?

sophia: Model refs: hf/cedar/custF-llama2-base, LoRAs: cedar-lora-v1 (bias-only), cedar-lora-v1.1 (full). They used our internal apply tool: `rw-lora apply --base hf/cedar/custF-llama2-base --lora cedar-lora-v1.1 --out cedar-merged-v1.1`

nora: Starting quick eval pack now on a c5-gpu smoke node. Using promptset: `cedar_quick_prompts_v1.json` (100 prompts, mix of QA/dialogue/emoji-heavy). Command: ```
rwinfer eval quick \n  --model cedar-merged-v1.1 \n  --quant int4 --quant-lib awq \n  --prompts ./cedar_quick_prompts_v1.json \n  --metrics em,bleu,perplexity,token_match \n  --out /tmp/cedar_quick_v1_3861234567.json
```

mx: I pulled the early run logs. Summary: EM -3.6 pts vs base, BLEU -2.1, perplexity +6.8%. Token_match (emoji) shows +0.8% mismatches; samples often drop trailing emoji or replace with <unk>.

sophia: paste example (expected vs actual):
EXPECTED: "I love it! 😄"
ACTUAL: "I love it!"

sam: Sounds like a tokenizer id/version mismatch or special_tokens table. Which tokenizer did Cedar use?

sophia: They claim `cedar-tokenizer-v2` (hf/cedar-tokenizer-v2). Our runtime on the smoke node uses tokenizers 0.15.3; cedar-tokenizer built with tokenizers 0.16.x. Could be detokenization differences.

aj: Short-term mitigation: run a tokenization normalization pass before eval: `python tooling/token_fix.py --add-emoji-mappings --input ...` or add missing emoji to special_tokens and retrain merge.

nora: Also tried a different quant path: AWQ-int4 vs QPack-int4. I ran qpack `--bits 4 --method smooth` and it degraded more (EM -5.1). AWQ is better here.

mx: Another datapoint: cedar-lora-v1 (bias-only) had almost no emoji mismatch but reduced task improvement. v1.1 (full) is where tokenization drop appears. Could be merged token remapping introduced by merge logic.

sophia: Customer wants both variants in staging. Proposal: 1) add tokenizer remap, 2) run AWQ-int4 quick eval, 3) run int8 baseline, 4) run 100-case behavior regression suite (customer prompts) and flag any EM drops >2 pts.

aj: Agreed. I'll script the remap step. Example snippet: ```
# remap unknown emoji to existing codepoints
python tooling/token_fix.py \n  --model-dir /mnt/models/cedar-merged-v1.1 \n  --add-special-tokens "['😄','👍','🤖']" \n  --save /mnt/models/cedar-merged-v1.1-fixed
```

sam: Kicking off staging job now (staging-runner-5). ETA ~20m :hourglass_flowing_sand: Will attach run id when ready.

deploy-bot: Deploy request created: deploys/3861234567 -> env: staging-runner-5, image: rwinfer:stable, note: cedar-lora-v1.1 quick-smoke

mx: If staging AWQ-int4 results are within thresholds we can canary to 10% with automatic fallback to base model on regressions. Verify rollouts: latency SLO @ 95th 300ms on our staging hardware.

sophia: Added to checklist and pinged customer with ETA. Also logging the path to results: `/artifacts/cedar/custF/3861234567/` — contains quick eval JSON + sample pairs.

sam: Run id: stag-3861234590 done. Uploading artifacts now. First look: AWQ-int4 EM -1.4 vs base, emoji token_match +0.05% (much improved). Full artifact: `/artifacts/.../awq-int4-report.json`

nora: Recommend next: rerun with full 1k-prompt eval overnight and include tokenization normalization as a control. I'll schedule that.

aj: I'll add a short unit test to our merge pipeline to check that special token tables are preserved across LoRA merges. If it fails, block merges and open a ticket.

sophia: Perfect — thanks everyone. Leaving the thread open until the 1k run finishes. :thumbsup:
